anchorLab.header.title: Character anchor lab
anchorLab.header.lead: Build an anchor set of a 3D character shot from the front, sides and back, then check on this device how closely AI-drawn candidates resemble it.
anchorLab.limits.title: Please read first
anchorLab.limits.score: The score is a heuristic reference that loosely compares colour distribution, palette, silhouette proportions and a structure hash. It does not decide whether two images show the same character.
anchorLab.limits.noGuarantee: Using anchors does not guarantee the same character in every cut. A different pose, lighting or framing can lower the score even for the same character.
anchorLab.limits.local: Images are never sent to a server and are processed only on this device. No face recognition or biometric extraction is used.
anchorLab.limits.virtualOnly: Use only images of virtual characters that you own or have permission to use. Do not upload photos of real people.
anchorLab.limits.stage: Capturing directly from the 3D stage is not connected yet. For now, drop images saved from 3D into each angle to build the set.
anchorLab.identity.title: 1. Anchor name and source character
anchorLab.identity.anchorId.label: Anchor id
anchorLab.identity.anchorId.hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 40 characters. Used in file names. Example: hero-01
anchorLab.identity.anchorId.error: Use only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and do not start or end with a hyphen. Enter it again like hero-01.
anchorLab.identity.characterId.label: Source character id
anchorLab.identity.characterId.hint: The id of the character this anchor was captured from. Letters, digits and . _ : - up to 64 characters. Example: char-7
anchorLab.identity.characterId.error: Start with a letter or digit and use only letters, digits and . _ : - up to 64 characters. Enter it again like char-7.
anchorLab.rights.title: 2. Rights confirmation
anchorLab.rights.confirm: These images show a virtual character that I own or have permission to use, and they are not photos or likenesses of real people.
anchorLab.rights.confirmHint: Check this to add images and download the set. The statement is also kept in the downloaded files.
anchorLab.rights.note.label: Source and permission note (optional)
anchorLab.rights.note.hint: Up to 300 characters. Kept in the rights record of the downloaded files.
anchorLab.rights.locked: Check the rights confirmation first. Images cannot be added until it is confirmed.
anchorLab.set.title: 3. Anchor set
anchorLab.set.lead: Drop one image into each of the six angles: front, left 3/4, left, back, right and right 3/4. Left and right follow the character's body. If one of a left/right pair is missing, only one side is referenced.
anchorLab.set.dropAll.hint: If a file name contains an angle word such as front, left, right, back or 3-4, the angle is guessed and placed for you. Please double-check guessed angles.
anchorLab.set.guessed: Guessed the angle of {count} files from their names. Please check they are right.
anchorLab.set.unassigned: {count} files with an unknown angle were not added. Drop them into a slot yourself.
anchorLab.set.accept: PNG, JPG or WebP, up to {max} MB each
anchorLab.set.recommend: Recommended: 2:3 portrait, {width}×{height}px, flat background, neutral pose
anchorLab.set.hashNote: The hash is computed only from the anchor id, source character id, angles and image contents. No timestamp is included, so identical images give an identical hash.
anchorLab.set.tooLarge: The set is {size} MB, over the {max} MB limit. Replace some images with smaller files and try again.
anchorLab.set.invalid: The set cannot be created. Check the anchor id and the images, then try again.
anchorLab.slot.dropHint: Drop an image or choose a file
anchorLab.capture.cancelledNote: Reading was cancelled. The {done} images already read are still here.
anchorLab.captureError.cancelled: Cancelled. Try again if you need it.
anchorLab.captureError.timeout: It took too long and was stopped. Check the file and try again.
anchorLab.captureError.fileEmpty: The file is empty. Choose another file.
anchorLab.captureError.fileTooLarge: The file is {size} MB, over the {max} MB limit per image. Choose a smaller file.
anchorLab.captureError.unsupportedFormat: Only PNG, JPG and WebP images can be used. Choose another file.
anchorLab.captureError.invalidDimensions: The image size cannot be read. Choose another file.
anchorLab.captureError.imageTooSmall: The image is only {width}×{height}px. Choose one whose shorter side is at least {min}px.
anchorLab.captureError.imageTooLarge: The image is {width}×{height}px, which is too large. Choose one whose longer side is at most {max}px.
anchorLab.captureError.decodeFailed: The image could not be opened. Check whether the file is damaged and try again.
anchorLab.captureError.sourceUnavailable: There is no file in this slot. Drop the file again.
anchorLab.captureError.sourceFailed: Something went wrong while reading the image. Try again in a moment.
anchorLab.captureError.invalidRaster: The image pixels could not be read correctly. Try again with another file.
anchorLab.captureError.rasterTooSmall: The image is too small to analyse. Choose one whose shorter side is at least {min}px.
anchorLab.captureError.rasterTooLarge: The image is too large to analyse. Choose a smaller image and try again.
anchorLab.captureError.emptyImage: The image has no visible pixels. Choose one that has non-transparent areas.
anchorLab.captureError.analysisHelper: The analysis helper could not start. Refresh the page and try again.
anchorLab.completeness.title: Set check
anchorLab.completeness.empty: There are no images yet. Drop images into the slots above.
anchorLab.completeness.clean: All six angles are present and there are no warnings to review.
anchorLab.completeness.usable: The front image is present, so the set can be used in a reference pack.
anchorLab.completeness.notUsable: Without a front image the set cannot be used in a reference pack. Drop a front image.
anchorLab.completeness.issue.missingMirr: {angle} is present but its pair {related} is missing. Only one side is referenced.
anchorLab.completeness.issue.sizeMismatc: The size of {angle} ({width}×{height}px) differs from the others ({expectedWidth}×{expectedHeight}px).
anchorLab.completeness.issue.aspectOffCo: The aspect ratio of {angle} ({width}×{height}px) differs from the recommended 2:3.
anchorLab.completeness.issue.belowRecomm: The longer side of {angle} is shorter than the recommended {recommended}px ({width}×{height}px).
anchorLab.export.title: 4. Download and reference pack
anchorLab.export.lead: Download the set as a ZIP with the images, set information, rights record and an AI composer reference pack document.
anchorLab.export.done: The ZIP was created and downloaded. It contains {count} files.
anchorLab.export.cancelled: Building the ZIP was cancelled. Try again if you need it.
anchorLab.export.error: The ZIP could not be created. Check the images and try again.
anchorLab.export.needIdentity: Enter a valid anchor id and source character id to download.
anchorLab.export.needRights: Check the rights confirmation to download.
anchorLab.export.needImages: Add at least one image to download.
anchorLab.export.contents: The ZIP contains images/, anchor-set.json, rights.json, reference-pack.json and README.txt.
anchorLab.pack.title: AI composer reference pack preview
anchorLab.pack.lead: This adds anchors as character references and shot pose/composition as method references to the existing image reference pack (v1). There is no direct import into the composer yet, so use the downloaded reference-pack.json.
anchorLab.pack.empty: The reference pack preview appears once the anchor id, rights confirmation and images are ready.
anchorLab.pack.usage: {character} character · {method} method · {total} in total (up to {max} at a time)
anchorLab.pack.skipped.title: Items left out of the reference pack
anchorLab.pack.reason.roleLimit: References for this role reached the limit ({max}).
anchorLab.pack.reason.providerLimit: The limit of images per request ({max}) was reached.
anchorLab.pack.reason.pairRule: There was no room for both images of a left/right pair, so the pair was skipped.
anchorLab.pack.reason.byteBudget: The total image size limit was reached.
anchorLab.pack.reason.invalidShot: The shot image information is not valid.
anchorLab.pack.reason.duplicateContent: A reference with the same content already exists.
anchorLab.pack.warning.missingFront: The front image is missing. Adding the front image first is recommended.
anchorLab.pack.warning.missingMirrorPair: Only {angle} is present without its pair {related}, so only one side is referenced.
anchorLab.shot.title: Shot pose and composition images (optional)
anchorLab.shot.lead: Adding pose and composition images saved from a 3D shot puts them in the reference pack as method references. The anchors carry identity; the guidance asks the model to use these only for pose and composition.
anchorLab.shot.id.label: Shot id
anchorLab.shot.id.hint: Letters, digits and . _ - up to 60 characters. Example: s1
anchorLab.shot.id.error: Start with a letter or digit and use only letters, digits and . _ - up to 60 characters. Enter it again like s1.
anchorLab.shot.needId: Enter a valid shot id to add images.
anchorLab.candidates.title: 5. Compare candidate images
anchorLab.candidates.lead: Compare AI-drawn candidates with the anchors to see a heuristic reference score and what differs. The score is only a reference and does not decide whether it is the same character.
anchorLab.candidates.needAnchor: Add at least one anchor image to compare candidates.
anchorLab.candidates.hint: PNG, JPG or WebP, up to {max} MB each, at most {count} images
anchorLab.candidates.limitReached: You can add up to {count} candidates. {skipped} were not added.
anchorLab.candidates.empty: There are no candidates yet. Drop candidate images to view them next to the anchors.
anchorLab.candidates.anchorFailed: The features of {count} anchor angles could not be calculated. Check those images and try again.
anchorLab.candidates.sort.label: Sort
anchorLab.candidates.sort.name: Name
anchorLab.candidates.sortNote: Candidates without a score always come last.
anchorLab.candidates.anchorSelect.label: Anchor to compare with
anchorLab.score.label: Heuristic reference score
anchorLab.score.bandNote: The band boundaries ({high} and {medium}) were chosen by people. They are neither an accuracy figure nor a pass/fail criterion.
anchorLab.score.disclaimer: This score loosely compares colour distribution, the overall dominant-colour palette, silhouette proportions and a structure hash. It does not decide whether it is the same character: a different pose, lighting or framing can lower it for the same character, and a similarly coloured but different drawing can score high.
anchorLab.score.limit.anchorNotSeparated: The subject could not be separated from the background in the anchor, so the whole image was compared. Silhouette comparison was left out.
anchorLab.score.limit.candidateNotSepara: The subject could not be separated from the background in the candidate, so the whole image was compared. Silhouette comparison was left out.
anchorLab.score.limit.anchorLowContrast: The anchor is almost one colour, so colour comparison is unstable.
anchorLab.score.limit.candidateLowContra: The candidate is almost one colour, so colour comparison is unstable.
anchorLab.score.limit.tinySubject: The subject is very small in the frame, so its features are unstable.
anchorLab.feature.title: Similarity by feature
anchorLab.feature.note: The palette compares only the dominant colours of the whole image, without assuming parts such as hair, skin or clothing. The weights were chosen by people.
anchorLab.compare.title: Side by side with the anchor
anchorLab.compare.empty: Select a candidate to view it next to the anchor.
anchorLab.compare.keys: Use the arrow keys in the candidate list: left or up for previous, right or down for next, Home and End for first and last.
anchorLab.compare.pending: This candidate has no score yet. It will appear here when analysis finishes.
anchorLab.diff.title: What differed
anchorLab.diff.note: These are statistical differences of the whole image. No parts such as hair, skin or clothing are assumed.
anchorLab.diff.none: No notable differences were found. That still does not mean it is the same character.
anchorLab.diff.lightness.brighter: The candidate is {delta} higher in average lightness (L*) than the anchor ({anchor} → {candidate}).
anchorLab.diff.lightness.darker: The candidate is {delta} lower in average lightness (L*) than the anchor ({anchor} → {candidate}).
anchorLab.diff.chroma.more: The candidate is {delta} higher in average chroma (C*) than the anchor ({anchor} → {candidate}).
anchorLab.diff.chroma.less: The candidate is {delta} lower in average chroma (C*) than the anchor ({anchor} → {candidate}).
anchorLab.diff.hue: The overall average hue differs by about {degrees}°.
anchorLab.diff.paletteMissing: The candidate has no colour close to the anchor's dominant colour {hex} ({percent}%). Its closest colour is {nearestHex} (colour difference ΔE {deltaE}).
anchorLab.diff.paletteExtra: The anchor has no colour close to the candidate's dominant colour {hex} ({percent}%). Its closest colour is {nearestHex} (colour difference ΔE {deltaE}).
anchorLab.diff.subjectScale.larger: The subject in the candidate is about {ratio}× larger than in the anchor.
anchorLab.diff.subjectScale.smaller: The subject in the candidate is about {ratio}× smaller than in the anchor.
anchorLab.diff.proportion.wider: The subject's width-to-height ratio is wider than the anchor's ({anchor} → {candidate}).
anchorLab.diff.proportion.narrower: The subject's width-to-height ratio is narrower than the anchor's ({anchor} → {candidate}).
anchorLab.diff.position: The subject moved {dxPercent}% horizontally and {dyPercent}% vertically (positive is right and down).
anchorLab.diff.silhouette: The subject outline differs a lot (silhouette similarity {percent}%).
anchorLab.diff.structure: The brightness structure hash differs a lot ({distance} of {bits} bits differ).
anchorLab.diff.nearDuplicate: Structure and colour are almost identical (structure hash differs by {distance} bits). Check whether the same picture was added again.
anchorLab.diff.subjectNotSeparated.both: The subject could not be separated from the background in either image, so the whole images were compared.
anchorLab.diff.subjectNotSeparated.ancho: The subject could not be separated from the background in the anchor, so the whole images were compared.
anchorLab.diff.subjectNotSeparated.candi: The subject could not be separated from the background in the candidate, so the whole images were compared.

branchingCuttoon.page.title: Branching cuttoon
branchingCuttoon.page.intro: An experimental tool to build a cuttoon whose story branches when readers pick a choice, and to preview it.
branchingCuttoon.page.limitsNote: There is no server storage, reader statistics or settlement yet. Your story is saved only in this browser, so export it as JSON and keep a copy.

guide.axis.rating.label: Top rated

guide.axis.trending.desc: Works with an exploding recent inflow

guide.diagram.reach.note: Even for the same “#1 on a platform”, the overall score differs by the scale of reach.

guide.example.body: Every platform's #1 sits near a popularity percentile of 100. By percentile alone they would all tie, so a small-platform work with large estimated metrics could accidentally take the overall #1. Applying reach weight and trust factor as multipliers changes the story. The numbers below compare only the core component of the popularity score (popComp): both works are serialized on a single platform (multi-platform bonus 1.00), and the trust factors are example values within range. The actual popularity score adds a rating adjustment and multiplies by freshness.
guide.example.caption: Bar lengths are proportional to the popularity component (popComp), based on 105
guide.example.note: Even for the same “#1 on a platform”, the popularity component differs by more than twofold. Small platforms are not ignored — they rise legitimately on other axes such as genre and hidden gems.
guide.example.title: Example: why the overall #1 is not a tiny-platform work
guide.honesty.measured: star ratings are collected real data
guide.honesty.mid1: . Since Naver made its view and interest counts private, some supporting metrics such as views and interest counts are shown as
guide.honesty.mid2: . The same applies to some ratings, views, and completion rates on other platforms. Estimates are always clearly marked with the
guide.honesty.mid4: above also reduces their influence on rankings. We never inflate prices or view counts.
guide.honesty.title: We never mix measured data with estimates
guide.how.heading: The four mechanisms behind the rankings
guide.how.note: Every axis is a combination of these four. See “View formula” in each step for the exact calculation.
guide.lede: No ToonStudio ranking is picked by hand. Rankings are calculated only from a published formula, and that formula is written out on this page — because you should be able to verify for yourself why a work sits where it does.
guide.pillar.bayes.body: Which should you trust: a 5.0 from 3 ratings, or a 4.6 from 10,000? The fewer the ratings, the more the score is pulled toward the overall average; as ratings accumulate, it approaches the work's true score.
guide.pillar.bayes.formula: bayes = (C×m + average rating×rating count) / (m + rating count) — C·m is derived from the catalog distribution
guide.pillar.bayes.title: Bayesian rating
guide.pillar.percentile.body: View counts use different units on every platform, so direct comparison is unfair. We first rank popularity within each platform, then make only the very top stand out.
guide.pillar.percentile.formula: popComp = 100 × exp((percentile−100)/2.5) × reach weight × trust factor × multi-platform bonus (1.00–1.06) — popularity score = (popComp + rating adjustment) × freshness
guide.pillar.percentile.title: Popularity percentile
guide.pillar.reach.body: Even for the same “#1 on a platform”, the actual reach (traffic scale) differs. Multiplying by platform scale makes the gap between major and small platforms clear.
guide.pillar.reach.formula: reach weight = the maximum among the platforms the work is serialized on
guide.pillar.reach.title: Reach weight
guide.pillar.trust.body: Values we actually collected count with confidence; values filled in by estimation count slightly less. This is the safeguard that keeps estimated metrics from pushing measured works out of #1.
guide.pillar.trust.title: Trust factor
guide.reach.desc: We use the largest value among the platforms a work is serialized on. It multiplies into the popularity and trending scores.
